context: Tatsuya-country tells Asuka about an old village proverb.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: あすか、昔の言葉、ようけある。
lines.en: Asuka, there are a lot of old words worth remembering.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Warm, reflective tone that settles into the words. Slight pause between name and thought, as if gathering decades of quiet observation. Steady breath, no rush.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.en: What kind of knowledge do you want to pass on?
lines.style: Gentle curiosity, leaning forward slightly with genuine interest. Soft voice, inviting him to continue. Warm without performing—the attention of someone who actually listens.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 寛容に生きる、長年、村の教え。
lines.en: Living with generosity—that's what the village has taught us over all these years.
lines.style: Quiet, almost meditative. Words chosen carefully, as if from long memory. Warm exhale on 「寛容に」. Pace slows on the ending, settling into the weight of the teaching.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 理不尽なこと、ようけある、世の中。
lines.en: There's so much unreasonableness in this world.
lines.style: Steady recognition, not complaint. Eyes present, acknowledging the truth without flinching. Soft but clear—the tone of someone who has seen difficulty and chosen kindness anyway.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: お互い、尊重して、生きるもんや。
lines.en: That's why we have to respect each other and just keep living.
lines.style: Firmer now, but not harsh. Conviction underneath, spoken as simple fact. The voice of someone who has lived this. Breath steady, gaze steady. A teaching, not an argument.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 若い人にも、伝えていきたいね。
lines.en: I want to pass that on to the younger generation too.
lines.style: Tender commitment. The word 「伝えていきたい」carries intention—not wistful, but determined. Soft voice building slightly on the resolve. Eye contact steady, warm.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.en: Yeah, that's a good way to be. You've got it right.
lines.style: Warm approval, almost quiet pride. A small nod in the voice—recognition of her stance without overselling it. Soft Tohoku inflection on the close. Breath easy, satisfied.
